s1.syndrome_frame: cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias in a patient with metastatic cancer
salient_findings: single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation identified on genetic analysis
key_facts: patient is a man in his 40s
patient has stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma
patient has pulmonary and liver metastases
patient has undergone radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus
genetic analysis was performed using paired whole-exome sequencing of affected tissue and patient's blood

raw.rationale: The lesion's characteristics, such as being a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias, and the presence of a KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation, are consistent with an atypical vascular lesion, particularly in the context of the patient's history of chemotherapy and radiation therapy.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Angiosarcoma typically presents with more aggressive features and is less likely to be a single, well-defined lesion.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Kaposi's sarcoma is often associated with immune suppression and has distinct histological features not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
rejected.why: Stewart-Treves syndrome is a type of lymphangiosarcoma that occurs in the context of chronic lymphedema, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Telangiectatic osteosarcoma metastasis
rejected.why: The patient's primary cancer is rectal adenocarcinoma, and there is no mention of osteosarcoma or bone metastases with telangiectatic features.

gold: Tufted angioma with somatic KDR mutation
